pr_title: Fix generating enum schema in gRPC JSON transcoding OpenAPI
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/51036

* Fix generating OpenAPI for enum when not nested inside message. Reuses `DescriptorRegistery` from `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Grpc.JsonTranscoding`.
* Fix `response_body` not being used when generating response schema
* Guard `MessageTypeInfoResolver` against being called with message interfaces by System.Text.Json

issue_context.title: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Grpc.Swagger Can't Deserialze Enum
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

If an enum is declared in the root of a proto file (not inside a message) you can't deserailze the the enum string to the proto enum. 

I have added a test case which shows the issue with this commit: https://github.com/cshaw-dmg/aspnetcore/commit/ad9ddaedbc9db9ee7885c3b7cc93db2e88a71b6d

### Expected Behavior

It should be possible to serialize/deserialize an enum even if it's at the root of the proto file.

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the test I added with this commit: https://github.com/cshaw-dmg/aspnetcore/commit/ad9ddaedbc9db9ee7885c3b7cc93db2e88a71b6d

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

_No response_

### Anything else?

The issue seems to be caused by this check: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Grpc/JsonTranscoding/src/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Grpc.Swagger/Internal/GrpcDataContractResolver.cs#L33

Because a root level enum isn't assignable to IMessage and because of that _enumTypeMapping is never populated with the enum's EnumDescriptor causing serialization to/from JSON to fail.

review_comments: I see this changed from `List` to `List`. Is that intentional?
Not intentional, but it doesn't matter. Swashbuckle generates the same output for IList and List.
Do we have test coverage for this change?

This change confused me. When I tested gRPC JSON transcoding in the sandbox app, the MessageTypeInfoResolver was called with interfaces by S.T.J. I haven't seen that before. Maybe it is new behavior in .NET 9, but on the other hand it doesn't show up in tests 🤷 

I guess I can add a unit test to verify.
